title: Global poverty reduction has stalled while climate and inequality risks remain geographically concentrated
source_unit: World Bank global poverty, prosperity, inequality, climate-risk, and data-coverage assessment
geography: Global, with regional and country-income-group comparisons

denominator.unit: global population poverty estimate using World Bank international poverty lines

extreme_poverty.unit: percent of global population living below $2.15 per day; almost 700 million people

poverty_685.unit: percent of global population living below $6.85 per day; around 3.5 billion people

low_income_poverty_direction.value: poverty rates in low-income countries are higher than before the pandemic

observations.method: World Bank Poverty, Prosperity, and Planet Report 2024 synthesis using household-survey-based global poverty and consumption/income estimates.
observations.uncertainty: Global estimates depend on survey coverage, purchasing-power adjustments, poverty-line definitions, interpolation, and country data availability; they are not US household estimates.
observations.subgroup: Global population, low-income countries, and the higher $6.85-per-day reference group.
observations.counterinterpretation: Aggregate poverty thresholds do not capture multidimensional wellbeing, informal support, public services, or within-country variation.

denominator.unit: global extreme-poverty population and World Bank regional/fragility classifications

sub_saharan_africa_extreme_poverty_share.unit: percent of people living in extreme poverty

fragile_conflict_affected_extreme_povert.unit: approximately percent of global extreme-poverty population when including fragile/conflict-affected countries

extreme_poverty_2030.unit: percent of global population projected to remain below $2.15 per day in 2030; 622 million people

poverty_685_2030.unit: nearly percent of global population projected below $6.85 per day in 2030; 3.4 billion people

observations.method: World Bank report regional concentration and current-trajectory projection; 2030 figures assume the report's baseline trajectory.
observations.uncertainty: The projection is scenario-dependent and sensitive to growth, conflict, distribution, population, survey updates, and policy; regional shares do not identify causal mechanisms within countries.
observations.subgroup: Sub-Saharan Africa, fragile/conflict-affected countries, and global population under the two poverty lines.
observations.counterinterpretation: Regional concentration can coexist with improvement in particular countries or communities; aggregate share is not individual persistence.

denominator.unit: World Bank global prosperity-gap and country inequality assessment

prosperity_gap.unit: Global Prosperity Gap relative to $25 per person per day

high_inequality_population.unit: approximately percent of world population living in countries with high inequality

upper_middle_income_years_to_close_gap.unit: years at current growth rates for a typical upper-middle-income country to close the Prosperity Gap

observations.method: World Bank shared-prosperity framework and cross-country inequality comparison; the Prosperity Gap emphasizes the distance of poorer populations from a $25-per-day threshold.
observations.uncertainty: The gap is an aggregate country-level indicator, not a direct measure of mobility, dignity, political trust, or within-country household experience.
observations.subgroup: Countries grouped by inequality and income level, with high inequality concentrated in Sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America/Caribbean.
observations.counterinterpretation: A country can reduce inequality without reaching the threshold, or grow rapidly while leaving particular groups behind; the indicator does not identify the policy path.

denominator.unit: World Bank global population risk and country household-survey availability frame

lifetime_extreme_weather_risk.unit: one in five people at risk of an extreme weather event in their lifetime

countries_with_recent_poverty_survey.unit: share of countries with a household survey available for poverty monitoring in 2020 or later

data_requirements.value: income/consumption distribution, spatial climate-risk exposure, and multidimensional poverty data

observations.method: World Bank report assessment of climate-risk exposure and the coverage/accessibility of household-survey data for poverty monitoring.
observations.uncertainty: Risk and data-coverage measures use different country and population frames; lack of a recent survey is not equivalent to poverty and reported exposure is not realized loss.
observations.subgroup: People exposed to extreme weather, countries with and without recent household surveys, and low-/middle-/high-income settings.
observations.counterinterpretation: Risk management, public services, social protection, and resilient assets can reduce realized livelihood loss even when hazard exposure is high.

boundary: This record contributes global poverty, shared prosperity, inequality, climate-risk, and data-coverage context to a US-centered comparative atlas. It does not estimate US household poverty, causal conflict effects, climate losses, political unrest, migration, legitimacy, or geopolitical behavior. Poverty thresholds, projections, regional shares, and data-coverage findings remain separate evidence types.
